Native DF 53.16 fortress depot trade text construction
===================================================

Static reconstruction from the two PE images configured in
data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. No game process or desktop was controlled.
Addresses below are reference-image RVAs unless an edition is named.
The retained .asm files contain the complete native instructions and branches.
Disassembler: configured w64devkit-2.9.1 native objdump.exe, Intel AMD64.

Renderer:
  Steam reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000, 0x384850..0x38a5b0.
  Official classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000, 0x382410..0x388170.
  Within this renderer, classic instruction RVAs = reference RVAs - 0x2440.
  Literal addresses are independent; native-sources.tsv retains both editions.
  Each edition has 97 printable literal references in the renderer.
  Executable reference return is 0x38a53a. The range after 0x38a53c is the
  29-entry switch table, not additional executable text branches.

Trade interface fields used by the native renderer:
  +0x48   talker string (merchant's short name)
  +0xb8   caravan_state pointer
  +0xc0   merchant civilization pointer
  +0xd0   merchant unit pointer
  +0xd8   fortress broker unit pointer
  +0x37a  int16 talkline (talk_line_type)
  +0x380  counteroffer item vector
  +0x398  counteroffer scroll position
  +0x3c0  big_announce vector of std::string* rows
  +0x3d8  big_announce scroll position
  +0x3dc  big_announce scrollbar interaction flag

Dialogue construction
---------------------

At 0x385be8 the renderer initializes a std::string to one ASCII quotation
mark. talkline is sign-extended at 0x385c00; unsigned values greater than 28
skip the switch. The selected branch appends one or more strings to this
same owner; 0x3861b9 appends the closing quotation mark. A native paragraph
split at 0x3861e5 calls 0x8e7310, then 0x386220..0x38626d draws its rows.
These strings are full quoted messages, not independently translatable words.

Reconstructed switch (table 0x38a53c):
  value  native branch  text construction
   0     0x385c24       Greet: five forms, expanded below
   1     0x385e88       "These goods are too heavy and cheap for me to consider."
   2     0x385e94       "I cannot take so much -- and at such cost!"
   3     0x385ea0       "Do not tempt me!  My beasts of burden cannot possibly haul such a load."
   4     0x385eac       "I wish I could take so much, but my animals..."
   5     0x385eb8       "I must make a profit.  There is simply not enough value here."
   6     0x385ec4       "I won't trade at a loss."
   7     0x385f70       "Ah, wonderful.  Thank you for your business."
   8     0x385f7c       ordinary: "I will see that our leader gets this offering."
                        nature-linked: "You are too kind."
   9     0x385fd2       "Take what you wish.  I can't stop you."
  10     0x385fde       ordinary: "You wish to make an offering to our leader?  This would please us greatly.  What do you offer?"
                        nature-linked: "You wish to make an offering?  We love gifts."
  11     0x386048       ordinary: "[Laughs uproariously]  You had me going there.  Obviously, your copious wit is matched only by your industry!"
                        nature-linked: "[Chuckles]  How droll."
  12     0x3860b2       "I am a merchant, yes.  You see, I wish to trade.  Which of my goods do you desire?"
  13     0x3860be       "Yes, and trade we will!  Simply tell me what interests you and what you're prepared to offer in exchange."
  14     0x3860dd       "Ah, but my goods are not free!  What do you offer in trade?"
  15     0x3860e9       "These _are_ fine items, aren't they?  Now, what do offer for them?"
  16     0x386108       "For me?  At no price?  I can accept your offer, or perhaps you wish to trade."
  17     0x386114       ordinary: "Are these gifts?  Do you wish to trade?"
                        same entity or same species: "My stones, are you giving me those?  Do you wish to trade or to make an offering to our leader?"
  18     0x38615b       "You truly despise life, don't you?  I am beside myself with grief.  Perhaps we will show you how they suffered."
  19     0x386193       "I see your low race still revels in death.  That poor, gentle creature..."
  20     0x386177       "Once a beautiful tree, and now?  It is a rude bauble, fit only for your kind."
  21     0x3861b9       only empty quotation marks
  22     0x3861b9       only empty quotation marks
  23     0x3861b9       only empty quotation marks
  24     0x385ed0       "Please understand the journey must be profitable.  Perhaps you'd consider tossing in a little extra?"
  25     0x385f32       "You'll need more goods to make this arrangement.  All I see here is not enough."
  26     0x385f51       "Even with your combined trade goods, such as they are, I can't fathom you ending up with the items you desire."
  27     0x385e22       nature-linked and caravan flag +0x20c0 bit0x80: "A hairy drunkard has come hither to once more disrespect the sanctity of life, I see."
                        otherwise: "What do you want?"
  28     0x385edc       ordinary: "Your childish games have made me tired.  Perhaps next time I visit you'll take this seriously."
                        nature-linked: "Leave it to the besotted dullard to miss the finer points of discourse.  I'm leaving.  Do reflect."

The repeated nature-linked predicate calls 0x75cfd0 on entity fields +0xcf2
and +0xcf4, also accepting +0xcf2 values 5 or 6. These are entity ethics
branches, rather than a translation decision based on a fixed race name.

Greet (case 0):
  if merchant entity ID (+4) == player entity ID (global 0x2393670):
    select "Greetings from the outer lands.  " or
           "Greetings from the Mountainhomes.  " by global byte 0x23912da;
    append "Your efforts are legend there.  Let us trade!".
  else if nature-linked:
    append "Greetings.  We are enchanted by ";
    append "your more ethical works.  We've come to trade.".
  else if merchant species (+0x98) == player species (global 0x239367c):
    append "Greetings from our mountain halls to yours.  Let us strengthen our bonds in trade.".
  else:
    append "Greetings.  The ";
    craft = broker RAW profession 25, queried through 0x30cea0/0x30cf70
            using broker species (+0xa4) and caste (+0x12c);
    fall back to "craftsman" if no broker or no RAW profession override;
    append craft + "ship of the ";
    append player creature RAW plural from 0xaa3bd0(player_species,plural=1,caste=-1);
    append " is unparalleled.  Let's make a deal!".

Thus case 0 has five full forms. Together with the six two-form cases,
the 26 nonempty switch slots contain 36 complete quoted dialogue forms.
Occupation and creature plural are term captures {s}; they are not civ names.
The normal paragraph splitter already retains full text and row addresses.

Merchant willingness
--------------------

The appraisal-skilled-broker condition is computed at 0x385b95..0x385bb5
using 0x133e7a0(unit,skill=0x48). If it holds, 0x3863dd copies the stored
talker name into a NEW std::string. It appends a predicate and final '.'
and draws the ENTIRE string once at 0x386538. It is not separate name and
predicate drawings; the formatter address binding belongs to a different owner.

score = caravan[+0x2118]. The seven actual branches are:
  score >=100: name + " seems ecstatic with the trading."
  score >=80 : name + " seems very happy about the trading."
  score >=60 : name + " seems pleased with the trading."
  score >=40 : name + " seems willing to trade."
  score >=20 : name + " seems to be rapidly losing patience."
  score >0   : name + " is not going to take much more of this."
  score <=0  : name + " is unwilling to trade."
Prefix selection uses the same threshold 20. Only those seven combinations
are native output; name is a typed {n} capture, including short first names.
The original threshold-specific foreground colors belong to the whole draw.

Counteroffer, controls and dynamic content
-----------------------------------------

When the counteroffer panel is active, 0x386691 and 0x3866de draw the fixed
two-row sentence "The following fortress goods were added for the counteroffer:".
Its translation owns both physical rows; they are not resolution-specific keys.
0x3867b5 draws Okay. Item labels are formatted separately from Value:/Weight:.
Native item formatters, instrument/item description grammars, material rules
and RAW vocabulary cover those dynamically generated labels and categories.
The raw literal table also retains Contains + count + item(s), Value:, Weight:,
Trader Profit:, Trader Loss:, Allowed Weight:, Excess Weight:, Mark all,
Unmark all, Seize, Accept Counteroffer, Trade and Offer as gift.
Numeric runs, currency glyphs and weight glyphs remain native fields.
Merchant-group names use the existing identity/entity formatters; the group
chooser, unloading apologies, readiness reply and no-merchants prompt are
already complete messages in the same authored UI catalog.

Artifact replies in big_announce
-------------------------------

Additional producer:
  reference 0x36a9c0..0x36b0a8; classic 0x368580..0x368c68.
  ABI: void(trade_interface*, item*, entity*, entity*, bool offer, bool seize).
  First four arguments are RCX/RDX/R8/R9; offer and seize are at entry
  RSP+0x28 and RSP+0x30. Retained assembly and artifact-sources.tsv
  describe both editions independently.

The helper requires the item, two entity pointers and merchant unit; the
entity must match interface.civ unless seize=true. It requires an artifact
item flag, a general_ref artifact entry and a nonempty artifact significance
vector (+0xc0, +0xd8 or +0xf0). It constructs these three complete messages:
  offer:
    "You honor " + entity_name(interface.civ->id) + " with the presentation of "
                 + artifact_name + "."
  else if seize:
    "Villains!  The seizure of " + artifact_name + " will not go unanswered."
  else:
    capitalize_first_byte(artifact_name) +
    " is a great treasure.  We respect that this is no mere trade."

entity_name is 0xb92900; artifact_name is 0xb94400. These fields use the
existing entity {e} and artifact {b} capture grammars. These paragraphs do
not receive the dialogue quotation wrapper.

Trade passes flags=0 to both name formatters. Entity names are English
language_name output (0xa946e0, translated=true) or "an unknown civilization".
Artifact names use the same English language_name output, without a native
name/quoted-gloss pair or item descriptor on the named branch. The remaining
artifact branches are "Untitled" for unnamed written objects, a complete
item descriptor (0xc65450) for ordinary unnamed artifacts, and "an unknown
artifact" for a missing record. The item fallback belongs to the artifact
capture too; arbitrary item names must not be treated as proper-name words.
The unnamed item branch uses mode 1, whose article virtual emits "the "
before quality, wear and decoration marks. The treasure reply changes it to
"The "; the rest of the item description retains its original case. A
capitalized generated title retains the existing proper-name grammar.

The complete string is built at stack [rbp-1] through 0x36accc. The helper
then manually wraps at 68 characters and appends allocated std::string* rows
directly to interface+0x3c0, inserting an empty separator between replies.
It does not call add_paragraph. At 0x36b01c it sets talkline=-1.
Renderer 0x38628d..0x38632a displays the visible slice of that vector,
with its own scrolling. Keeping only visible rows loses message identity
when the first row or the artifact name has scrolled out of view.

The original full string remains at [rbp-1]. At 0x36ad21 the native copy
function 0x6f8d0 receives its pristine byte pointer (RDX), length (R8) and
allocated destination (RCX), with the interface still held in R12. The
wrapper only mutates the copied temporary string, including inserting a
space inside words longer than 68 bytes at 0x36ae1a..0x36ae33. Concatenating
final rows with spaces therefore cannot always reconstruct the source.
At 0x36b007 the temporary vector is destroyed after the final row was
appended; R12 has been restored to the interface. These two specific calls
provide source capture and completion without hooking a shared string
operation throughout the game. The completion can associate only the new
message's actual row addresses with its pristine source.

Callers 0x31bf96 (offering), 0x31af52 (seizing) and transaction 0x36a5d7
(accepted trade; 0x36a307 is the other shared transaction path) reach this
producer. Other direct big_announce global references in 0x3153ba..0x316125
and 0x8b7550..0x8b7653 read row counts or modify scroll position. They do
not construct an additional text family.

Authored translations are in data/runtime/ui-messages.tsv. Exact full-message
provenance is appended to data/extracted/ui-message-sources.tsv. Source literal
tables preserve the individual native fragments without treating them as
standalone translation keys.
